questions.question: How does the brightness of two identical bulbs connected in parallel compare to the same two bulbs connected in series using the same battery?
options: The bulbs in parallel are dimmer than the bulbs in series.
The bulbs in parallel are brighter than the bulbs in series.
The bulbs in parallel have the exact same brightness as the bulbs in series.
The bulbs in parallel do not light up at all, while the series ones do.

questions.question: If you connect two identical bulbs to a battery in parallel, how does the total current compare to when they are connected in series to the same battery?
options: The current in the parallel circuit is bigger.
The current in the series circuit is bigger.
The current is exactly the same in both circuits.
No current flows in the parallel circuit at all.

questions.question: When using the same battery, how does the voltage across one of two bulbs connected in parallel compare to the voltage across one of two bulbs connected in series?
options: The voltage across a bulb in parallel is smaller than across a bulb in series.
The voltage is zero across both bulbs in both circuits.
The voltage across a bulb in parallel is bigger than across a bulb in series.
The voltage is exactly the same across a single bulb in both setups.

questions.question: What will happen to the lifespan of a battery if it is used to light two bulbs in parallel compared to lighting the same two bulbs in series?
options: The battery lighting the parallel circuit will run out faster.
The battery lighting the series circuit will run out faster.
Both batteries will run out in the exact same amount of time.
The battery in the parallel circuit will last infinitely longer.

questions.question: In physics, what does electrical resistance measure?
options: The rate at which electric charge is created inside a cell.
How difficult it is for an electric current to flow through a material.
The speed at which voltage travels along a wire.
The total number of batteries connected in a closed circuit.

questions.question: How does the length of a wire affect its electrical resistance?
options: A longer wire has less resistance.
The length of a wire does not affect its resistance.
A longer wire has a greater resistance.
Only the first few centimeters of a wire have resistance, regardless of length.

questions.question: If you double the length of a uniform conducting wire, what happens to its electrical resistance?
options: Its resistance is halved.
Its resistance doubles.
Its resistance remains completely unchanged.
Its resistance quadruples.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the electrical resistance of a uniform wire and its length?
options: Resistance is proportional to length.
Resistance is inversely proportional to length.
Resistance is proportional to the square root of length.
There is no mathematical relationship between resistance and length.

questions.question: Which of the following best defines electrical power?
options: The total amount of electrical force stored inside a battery.
The measurement of how many electrons are inside a wire at any moment.
A measure of the amount of energy used by or supplied to a device in one second.
The time it takes for a current to travel all the way around a circuit.

questions.question: What unit is used to measure electrical power?
options: Ohms (Ω)
Amps (A)
Volts (V)
Watts (W)

questions.question: How are electricity bills calculated in terms of energy units used?
options: Every 1 unit of energy on a bill is equal to 1 kilowatt-hour (kWh).
Every 1 unit of energy on a bill is equal to 1 watt-second (Ws).
Every 1 unit of energy on a bill is equal to 1 amp-hour (Ah).
Every 1 unit of energy on a bill is equal to 1 volt-ampere (VA).

questions.question: What is a parallel circuit?
options: A circuit with only a single, unbroken loop from one end of a battery to the other.
A circuit with more than one complete loop from one end of a battery to the other.
A circuit where electrons can only flow in a backward direction.
A circuit that requires multiple batteries connected in opposite directions to function.

questions.question: In a parallel circuit, how does the current through each individual branch relate to the total current through the battery?
options: The current in each branch is always double the total current through the battery.
The current through each branch adds up to the total current through the battery.
The current through each branch is exactly equal to the total current through the battery.
The total current through the battery is divided by the square of the number of branches.

questions.question: How does the thickness of a wire affect its electrical resistance?
options: The thicker a wire, the smaller its resistance.
The thicker a wire, the greater its resistance.
The thickness of a wire has no effect on its resistance.
Thicker wires only have resistance when heated to extreme temperatures.

questions.question: What happens to the electrical resistance of a wire if its cross-sectional area is doubled?
options: Its resistance is doubled.
Its resistance is halved.
Its resistance remains the same.
Its resistance is quartered.

questions.question: How does the voltage across each branch of a parallel circuit compare to the voltage across the power source (cell or battery)?
options: It is equal to the voltage across the cell or battery.
It is divided equally among the branches so each branch gets a fraction.
It is always double the voltage of the cell or battery.
It is zero across all branches.
